assumptions: SLATE models no advance payments: the whole premium is paid and the credit taken on the return, as for every marketplace plan in SLATE; so "advance" eligibility is read as the credit's and Covered Connecticut's.
Every SLATE life is unmarried, so the joint-filing rule never bars it.
The status is read at the year's end, for the year (an annual approximation: a status that changes mid-year isn't reached).

No played F-1 life pays marketplace premiums in 2026 (her status ends within weeks of a withdrawal, a personal leave is refused her, OPT comes after the degree in 2029), so this is reached on a FIXTURE only.

sources.rule: 42 CFR 435.550-563: applicable individual 19 to under 65 (435.551); monthly income is MAGI-based income, earned and unearned (435.552(f)(2)); mandatory exceptions incl. under 19 (435.553); specified excluded incl. health.dental.corrected.now: SLATE sells the New Haven student one dental plan, Yale’s, its year paid at once (dentalPlanFor); New York’s and California’s monthly plans are for lives in those states, which no new life lives, so they’re fixtures here. Through the command on the student, Yale’s plan is bought for its plan year, to 1 October (defects-g8-4.test.ts:239-250), leaves a cleaning free (teethAndEyesShareOf), and can’t be canceled once paid (costs.test.ts:220-223). What isn’t checked on it: the year’s price taken from the current account, a filling past its deductible to its $1,000 maximum (tested on New York’s plan alone, costs.test.ts:151-167), and the plan read past its end; that it outlives the degree is tested with healthMonth called by hand (defects-g8-4.test.ts:258-261). The monthly plans’ premium and ending are tested by calling healthMonth on a plan put in (defects-g8-4.test.ts:267-269, costs.test.ts:178-179). Partial on the student’s own plan, for the year’s price.
